components.css: .ds-profile{background:var(--color-paper,#f6f6f4);color:var(--color-ink,#101012);padding:24px;font-family:"Pretendard Variable",Pretendard,sans-serif;max-width:360px}.ds-profile h3{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:baseline;gap:10px;margin:0;font-size:29px;font-weight:800;letter-spacing:-.025em}.ds-profile h3 span{font-size:14px;font-weight:500;color:var(--color-muted,#64645f)}.ds-profile blockquote{margin:17px 0 24px;font-size:16px;line-height:1.7}.ds-profile-details{border-top:1px solid var(--color-ink,#101012);border-bottom:1px solid var(--color-divider,#c7c7c2)}.ds-profile-details summary{display:flex;min-height:56px;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;gap:16px;list-style:none;font-size:14px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer}.ds-profile-details summary::-webkit-details-marker{display:none}.ds-profile-details summary:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--color-accent,#d10e1c);outline-offset:4px}.ds-profile-details summary:focus-visible{outline-offset:-3px}.ds-profile-close{display:none}.ds-profile-details[open] .ds-profile-open{display:none}.ds-profile-details[open] .ds-profile-close{display:inline}.ds-profile-indicator{position:relative;width:16px;height:16px;flex-shrink:0}.ds-profile-indicator:before,.ds-profile-indicator:after{content:"";position:absolute;left:1px;top:7px;width:14px;height:2px;background:currentColor}.ds-profile-indicator:after{transform:rotate(90deg);transition:transform .2s ease}.ds-profile-details[open] .ds-profile-indicator:after{transform:rotate(0)}.ds-credentials{padding:8px 0 24px}.ds-credentials h4{font-size:16px;font-weight:800;margin:0}.ds-credentials ul{display:grid;gap:7px;margin:9px 0 0;padding-left:15px;list-style:disc;font-size:14px;line-height:1.8;color:var(--color-secondary-text,#51514d)}@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-profile-indicator:after{transition-duration:.01ms}}

narrative.overview:
A trainer speaks in large black and red type, beside an original color portrait. The visual character comes from a printed stage page: condensed weight, a slight rotation, real ink wear, and a clear speaker. Calm neutral space and plain service information make that expressive voice usable for a local gym.

Photography supplies the evidence. Keep the actual trainers, facility photographs, and U mark recognizable. The page gives membership and PT consultation equal visual weight. It uses a strong first statement, then straight photographic sections and readable profiles; the expressive material does not turn every paragraph into a poster.
keyCharacteristics: Black display type with red emphasis on a light neutral field.
Original color portraits and real facility photography.
Printed wear confined to the lead quotation and paired consultation backgrounds.
Flat, square photographic sections with small control corners.
Clear booking and phone actions, including a green Naver action on mobile.

rules.name: The Service Color Rule
rules.body: Keep Naver green attached to Naver booking. General page emphasis remains black and red.

rules.name: The Speaker Rule
rules.body: Keep the large quotation as selectable semantic text with an adjacent attribution. The ink mask is a decorative layer, never an image replacement for the words.

rules.name: The Flat Evidence Rule
rules.body: Let real photographs and type establish the hierarchy. Keep profile, program, and facility content flat rather than lifting it into repeated floating cards.

dos: Do preserve original color trainer portraits, real facility photographs, and the vector U identity.
Do keep membership and PT consultation equal in width and visual importance.
Do use the supplied local display and body fonts with the observed role separation.
Do keep the lead quotation selectable, attributed, and linked in meaning to the real profile.
Do preserve keyboard focus, native profile disclosure, reduced motion, safe-area spacing, and a direct map fallback.
Do use confirmed names, credentials, contact details, and service facts from the product sources.
donts: Don't replace real people or facilities with generated or stock evidence, fabricated testimonials, or invented performance claims.
Don't desaturate the user-approved original color portraits.
Don't turn printed wear into a treatment for body copy, profile credentials, or control labels.
Don't add floating-card shadows, pill-shaped photo frames, or repeated reveal effects to the flat sections.
Don't use Naver green as a general brand accent.
Don't invent prices, discounts, parking terms, or round-the-clock consultation staffing from the confirmed 24-hour gym operation.
